title: --help flow: option parse to callback to formatter
answers: How is --help output produced in click?
Where is the help option created and registered?
body:
All paths in src/click/.
1. core.py:Command.main → Command.make_context → Command.parse_args → make_parser, which loops core.py:Command.get_params(ctx) and calls param.add_to_parser.
2. core.py:Command.get_params appends core.py:Command.get_help_option(ctx) to self.params. The help option is created lazily and cached in a private attr.
3. core.py:Command.get_help_option_names takes ctx.help_option_names (default --help) minus names already used by params. It returns None if there are no names or add_help_option is False.
4. The option's callback is decorators.py:show_help. It is invoked during parsing and echoes ctx.get_help(), then ctx exits.
5. core.py:Context.get_help calls Command.get_help(ctx) → format_help, which writes the sections through a HelpFormatter from ctx.make_formatter().
6. Command.get_usage(ctx) uses format_usage the same way.
The section writers live in formatting.py: HelpFormatter.write_usage, write_text, write_dl, section.
The trace only partially shows the format_help internals (output truncated), so verify the order of format_* calls.
